title: Routing Basics
description: Learn the fundamentals of client-side routing with React Router.

data.text: **React Router** is the standard routing library for React. It enables navigation among views in a single-page application (SPA) by changing the browser URL and rendering the matching component without a full page reload.
Install `react-router-dom` — the DOM bindings for React Router. It includes BrowserRouter, Routes, Route, Link, and more.
Wrap your app in `<BrowserRouter>`. Inside, use `<Routes>` and `<Route>` to map paths to components. Use `<Link>` for navigation instead of `<a>` tags.

data.title: Router Setup
React Router Components
items: **BrowserRouter** — Provides routing context using the HTML5 history API.
**Routes** — Container that holds all Route definitions.
**Route** — Maps a URL path to a component element.
**Link** — Navigation component that changes the URL without reloading the page.

data.text: Always use `<Link>` for internal navigation. `<a>` tags cause a full page reload and lose React state. Use `<a>` only for external URLs.

data.text: Use a `path="*"` route at the end of your Routes list to handle unknown paths.

data.title: Exercise: Build a Navbar with Routes
data.description: Create a navigation bar with three links and route them to separate pages.
steps: Create Home, About, and Contact page components.
Add a Navbar with Links to each page.
Add a NotFound page for unknown routes.
data.expectedOutcome: A navigable SPA with three pages and a 404 fallback.

items.question: Why does my page reload when I click a Link?
items.answer: Check that you wrapped the app in BrowserRouter and used <Link>, not <a>.

items.question: What version of React Router should I use?
items.answer: Use React Router v6+. It uses element props instead of component props and has a simpler nested route API.

items.question: Can I use React Router with Next.js?
items.answer: Next.js has its own file-system router. If you use Next.js App Router, you typically do not need react-router-dom.

items.question: How do I pass query parameters?
items.answer: Use useSearchParams (v6.4+) or read window.location.search for simple cases.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: React Router enables SPA navigation without page reloads.
Use BrowserRouter, Routes, and Route to define URL mappings.
Use Link for internal navigation; use a for external links.
Add a path='*' route to handle 404 pages.
data.takeaway: Routing turns your React app into a navigable multi-page experience. Next, you will explore nested routes for shared layouts.
